exposure: Lower uterine segment (LUS) stiffness measured by ultrasound elastography (point Shear Wave Elastography (pSWE) and bidimensional Shear-Wave-Elastography (2D-SWE))
outcome: Correlation between US elastography measurements of LUS stiffness and tensile-stress-strain-rupture analysis
cohort: 33 women with a previous cesarean section undergoing repeat cesarean section
finding: Ultrasound elastography, particularly 2D-SWE, showed promise in determining the viscoelastic properties of the lower uterine segment in women with a previous cesarean section, with a strong correlation found between 2D-SWE measurements and tensile-stress-strain analysis (r=0.78, p<0.001).
